significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish a form-(iii) behavioral law—that the measurable endorsement lift from repetition has a small interaction with measured source credibility, so “distrusted-source repetition still inflates endorsement”—together with a form-(ii) mechanism in which separable familiarity and credibility signals are weakly coupled and familiarity causally drives the lift. This would fix expectations for source-attributed, repeated claims beyond the individual examples and would distinguish repetition-driven context dependence from the user-opinion dependence documented by Sharma et al., “Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models” (ICLR 2024). It establishes both a weighty phenomenon and a causal account; the negative branch is also informative because strong moderation would establish source-sensitive epistemic gating, although failure of the proposed ablation would only reject the specific mechanism. True and false outcomes are determinate through the “repetition x credibility interaction,” and the topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: a generic claim that query context affects retrieval lacks this specific interaction law and two-signal account.

reach.justification: The named handles are the “repetition x credibility interaction” as an auditing diagnostic and the “credibility-gating steering” intervention; the former is largely post hoc, while the latter is ex ante because it can suppress an untrusted repetition effect before the model issues its verdict. After per-model re-extraction, the hypothesis predicts a substantive relation—a small credibility moderation of the familiarity-to-verdict slope—and not merely a procedure for searching, although the particular low-rank steering direction would still require local calibration. The asserted scope covers several model families and factual domains, including health misinformation, and the downstream users could include factuality evaluators and practitioners gating source-attributed assistants, but the claim does not establish transfer to frontier models or unrestricted dialogue. The topic-substitution check lowers no further: deleting the specific diagnostic, interaction, and steering handle leaves only a broad knowledge-retrieval topic that would not justify practitioner uptake or ex-ante lead time.
